text: Theorem 2 proves diffusion models require O~(ε^-(k∨2)) samples to achieve ε-accuracy in 1-Wasserstein distance, where k is the intrinsic (subspace) dimension rather than the ambient dimension d (Section 3.2, Theorem 2).
Theorem 1 bounds the score estimation L2 error in terms of the intrinsic dimension k, avoiding the exponential dependence on ambient dimension d found in prior analyses (Section 3.2, Theorem 1).

The analysis assumes the target distribution's support lies in a union of M low-dimensional linear subspaces with zero probability mass on their intersections, and requires only subgaussian tails within each subspace (Section 2.2, Assumption 1).
The results dispense with smoothness (e.g., Hölder continuity), log-concavity, uniform density bounds, and density lower-bound assumptions required by prior sample-complexity analyses (Section 2.2).
Prior work requiring β-Hölder smooth densities achieves only ε^-(d+2β)/β sample complexity, exhibiting a curse of dimensionality that the paper's bound avoids (Section 1, Equation 1).
